part2_ceilingScreen.whyEveryOtherCompFails: One fast weapon is enough to saturate. Per-unit max rate = 60 / the unit's tightest observed credit gap: MG ~60/s, SMG 20/s, AR 12/s, SG 1.5/s, SR/RL/charge 0.64-1.0/s. Five slow units sum to ~3-5/s; a single MG or SMG carrier puts the comp at or past the cap on its own.
part2_ceilingScreen.sharpEdgeWorthKnowing: The ceiling is a MAX-rate statistic driven by a unit's single tightest gap, so ONE coincident credit pair pins that unit at 60/s regardless of its weapon — jill is an AR with a measured 2.5 pulls/s cadence override and still scores 60/s off a single 1-frame gap. 'Slow weapons' is therefore necessary but not sufficient; the screen must be RUN, not predicted from the roster.

correctionToAnEarlierRecordingAsk: An earlier statement of this ask said 'five slow-firing units - SR / RL / charge / AR, no MG and no SMG'. Including AR was WRONG: AR scores 12/s per unit, so even two AR carriers plus three slow units reach ~26/s and leave the detector no room. The screen's own numbers are the correction. caveats: FEASIBILITY ONLY. No classification, no branch, no stamp, no engine or constant change.
The ceiling is a sim-side property; a non-vacuous ceiling means the detector CAN fire, not that it WILL.
The reader smoke test covers a 40s slice, not the full 198s fight; a real run must read all windows.

N3's measured FB count is 10 vs sim 10 (matrix status 'disabled'), so it is NOT a comp with a known rotation shortfall - what it offers is an independent ceiling test, not a second copy of iron sweep's gap.
N5 is reported for completeness; its ceiling 15.87 leaves little power and it should not be treated as a peer candidate.
